# دليل العمرة الشامل — Umrah Checklist

> An interactive, offline-first Umrah checklist in 10 languages. One HTML file,
> zero dependencies, zero build step. Covers the rites in performance order from
> the mīqāt to taḥallul, with ṭawāf/saʿī counters, duʿās, iḥrām prohibitions, and
> the five mīqāt locations. Free, open source, no accounts, no tracking.

- Live: https://nouraldeentofi.com/umrah-guide/
- Source: https://github.com/nouraldeentofi/umrah-checklist
- Author: Nour Aldeen Tofi — https://nouraldeentofi.com
- Code license: MIT. Content: free to redistribute, not to sell. See CONTENT-NOTICE.md

## What it covers

The eight phases of Umrah, 35 steps in performance order:
1. Preparation and iḥrām at the mīqāt (ghusl, garments, prayer, intention, conditional intention)
2. The talbiyah on the way to Makkah
3. Entering al-Masjid al-Ḥarām
4. Ṭawāf — seven circuits (idṭibāʿ, raml, the Black Stone, the Yemeni corner)
5. After ṭawāf — two rakʿahs at Maqām Ibrāhīm, Zamzam
6. Saʿī between Ṣafā and Marwah — seven laps
7. Ḥalq or taqṣīr, and release from iḥrām
8. Iḥrām prohibitions and the five mīqāt locations

## Languages

Arabic (default), English, Urdu, Hindi, French, Spanish, Spanish (Argentina),
Filipino, Japanese, Chinese. Contributions of further languages are welcome —
see CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Religious basis

Follows the Ḥanbalī madhhab as taught and practised in the Ḥaramayn, checked
against the fatwas of Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn and Shaykh Ibn Bāz. Known differences
are noted rather than hidden (e.g. ḥalq/taqṣīr is a wājib for the majority and a
rukn in the Shāfiʿī school). This is a checklist and study aid, not a fatwa.

The first draft was written with LLM assistance, then put through two review
passes against published references. The primary source is Dalil al-Mu'tamir,
compiled by Talal ibn Ahmad al-'Aqil, published by the Committee for the
Distribution of Religious Publications to Pilgrims (Jeddah, 1426 AH,
ISBN 9960-49-505-1) — the official booklet distributed to pilgrims in the
Haramayn. Every correction is documented in REVIEW.md. Human scholarly review
is still outstanding. See CONTENT-NOTICE.md for the full source list.

## Notable engineering

- Read-aloud via Web Speech API: du'as spoken in ar-SA at reduced rate, step
  explanations spoken in the selected locale; voice resolution falls back from
  exact BCP 47 tag to language prefix. No audio files, works offline.
- Text-size control (3 levels), persisted
- 10 locales across 5 writing systems with per-script typography and font stacks
- Runtime bidirectional layout — `dir` flips on the same DOM, nothing duplicated
- Locale-aware numerals (Arabic-Indic ٠-٩, Eastern Arabic ۰-۹)
- Self-contained export: clones the live DOM, serialises the Arabic i18n base
  into an injected script, emits a standalone multilingual HTML file with state
- Three-tier storage fallback (window.storage → localStorage → memory), 7-day TTL
- PWA: cache-first shell, stale-while-revalidate font caching for offline use
- JSON-LD HowTo + WebApplication structured data
- ~200 KB total, single file, no dependencies, no build
